spans.s:
Kraivya. Pāñcāla, the king of the Krivis,^1 is mentioned in
the Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa^2 as having performed the Aśvamedha,
or horse sacrifice, on the Parivakrā. Eggeling,^3 however,
takes the word as a proper name, ‘Kraivya, the Pāñcāla king.’
1) So the St. Petersburg Dictionary,
s.v.; Weber, Indian Literature, 125, n.;
Oldenberg, Buddha, 409, n.
2) xiii. 5, 4, 7.
3) Sacred Books of the East, 44, 397
(but cf. p. 398, top).
